g.text: LANDED 2026-09-25, and this note corrects a first version that said
otherwise. That version claimed the RTL did not exist, measured in THIS
worktree -- which is behind main, where the landed control lives (21
references in pe_ctrl.v, 8 in pe_cpu.v). The lesson is the one this project
keeps paying for: a local measurement is not a project claim, and the eight
"missing" persona acts had already been caught the same way in the same
THE BRING-UP TRAP is the part a host must design around: once the core is
HELD, the run strap is ignored BOTH WAYS. A hold is released only by
(pe_cpu.v:233). A host that single-steps or hits a breakpoint and then
re-asserts run=1 to carry on finds the core STILL HELD, with no fault and
nothing in the response words to explain it.
THE === FORM IS THE CONTRACT, not decoration. An UNDRIVEN debug input then
reads as INACTIVE; the plain !dbg_hold form propagates x and freezes the core
at reset. The convention is enforced where the input is consumed rather than
at every call site, which is the only place a new call site cannot forget it.
Leaving those inputs undriven took six acts to their reset after the 5b4731f
The architectural point of the whole firmware-protocols effort: these are not
peripherals. They are PROGRAMS on the same CPU, pin matrix and tick, which is
why a rate the 260-CLOCK UART half-bit tick cannot express (MIDI 31.25 kbaud,
DMX 250 kbaud) is still reachable -- by counting instructions. Measured on
the pin: MIDI 31,998.7 ns / 31,251 baud and DMX 3,999.8 ns / 250,010 baud,
both with zero spread across every frame.
NAME THE TICK beside any conclusion drawn from it. This SoC has TWO tick
counters and they are not the same size: port 7 (STATUS) is the UART
HALF-BIT tick at 260 clocks / 4.33 us, and port 4 (I2CTICK) is a
free-running 1 us counter built from I2C_TICKS = CLK_HZ / 1_000_000 = 60
exactly (pe_soc.v:560), so it has no rounding error at all. So "the tick
cannot express a fraction" is true of the 260-clock tick and FALSE of the
1 us one, which divides 4.3333 us only inexactly but 4.000 us exactly. The
acts here count instructions rather than program either tick, so nothing in
this section depends on which one is meant -- but a reader who is not told
which tick will carry the wrong conclusion into their own act.
THE REMAINING RED. Everything above is simulated and mapped; the physical
Pico/USB board acceptance is the one item no simulation can close.
A COUNT IS AN ASSERTION, so the two numbers in this section are deliberately
NOT the same kind of thing and must not be conflated:
* 10 PROPERTIES across 5 modules is what formal/results/summary.txt
records, and it stays 10. Do not let a larger target count overwrite it.
* 11 TARGETS is that same 10 plus the SMT unlock below.
The unlock exists because the built-in `sat -tempinduct` is a self-contained
k-induction over a sampling netlist in which a register's next-value is
DUPLICATED per sampling domain, which is why four pe_ctrl claims looked
toolchain-blocked. write_smt2 + yosys-smtbmc/z3 gives each register ONE
next-value function. It also validates the pipeline: the known-inductive
pe_ctrl subset passes there too, so a FAILED run on a hard claim means the
29 figures across 13 act families, on a deliberate naming convention: the
bare `proto-<act>` is the act's own figure, and `-frame` and `-timing` split
it into the encoding layer and the cell/cadence layer. Seven acts carry all
three (dht11, ds18b20, fm-biphase, freqmeter, nec-ir, servo, sr04); the other
six carry the bare figure only, because those acts have one story to tell
rather than two layers over it.
The maps name the whole convention rather than listing 29 nodes, because a
list that long stops being a map. What matters for a reader is that the
family exists, what its three members mean, and that the act list is
The three figures are the wire contract drawn, and each is built from the
RTL rather than from the prose: the response builders, the dbg_state
equation, the hit latch and the execute gate. proto-spi-framing carries the
word/bit layout and the WAIT-WORD rule; proto-r2-read-path the 11-word
header field by field and the read-count ceiling; proto-r3-debug-control
the state machine, STOP-BEFORE and the masked run strap.
The six concept pages behind them are wiki/concepts/host-chip-protocol,
soc-wiring-and-memory. The maps name all six so the documentation surface
is not understated: a page that exists but that no map points at is a page
the next reader will not find.
HC-SR04 ranging is PLANNED, and is the one firmware act whose testbench is
not wired into run_all.sh -- so a green suite is currently SILENT about it.
Measured standalone 2026-09-25: 5 checks fail. See the progress map, which
records the measurement rather than the intention.
Baseline firmware personas: UART, SPI master, I2C master.
The passive loader is a separate SPI path used to load instruction SRAM.
Current aliases: uo_out[0] is UART TX / SPI SCLK; ui_in[0] is UART RX /
SPI MISO; uio[0:1] are I2C SDA/SCL; uio[2:3] are SPI MOSI/CS_N.
ui_in[2] is 10BASE-T RX; uo_out[2] is 10BASE-T TX (G6 reclaim of dbg_pc[0]).
The Linux GUI and its PC-to-board transport are planned software; the
transport and control API are not chosen yet. The RP2040 sits on the Tiny
Tapeout demo board and is the chip-side SPI host.
Landed 2026-09-24 (manager decision): the R1 framed host bus supersedes the
A1 raw uio[4] echo — SPI mode 0, MSB-first 16-bit words, 16'hA55A sync,
CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE, response opcode bit 7, sequence/target echoed; the
commit-latched word echo lives in the framed LOAD response. Pads: uio[4:7]
CS_N/MOSI/MISO/SCK, uo_out[1] = IRQ_N (sticky, active low), ui_in[3:5]
freed; 19 of 24 committed. See wiki/plans/host-controller-gui.md and
Landed 2026-09-24: ONE pe_serdes with split payload-only enables (TX
advances only on payload cells, serdes.tx_bit_en = tx_codec_cell_en &&
!tx_stuffed; RX captures only payload cells, serdes.rx_bit_en =
rx_codec_cell_en && rx_bit_valid). TWO unmodified pe_codec_mux instances are
independent 2x half-cell LEVEL; the pad overlay sits before the matrix's
open-drain gate, and a latched-phase window on port 0xF has
separate TXLEN/RXLEN. First consumer is the wire loopback (plain and stuffed
Manchester, word 0x07E0) through TX codec, simulation wire model, DRU/codec
RX, and SERDES RX; a trailing stuff cell is covered by construction. The
10BASE-T TX frame consumer (pe_eth_tx) is integrated below and shares the
TX codec through the tx_path owner mux. Landed 2026-09-25 (plan Tasks 1-5):
full frame from firmware pushes, 32-entry window, owner mux, G6 uo_out[2]
pad, loopback acceptance PASS (FCS 9cc5cb34, IFG 102 cells). Plan Tasks 6
Low-speed USB and CAN are later personas; JTAG, SWD, and PS/2 are optional.
A1 word echo; one frame late
board connections, including optional SPI MISO
